observations.predicate: is described as / referred to by the acronym
observations.subject: order of add/remove of stack elements

claims.rationale: 引文（区间 [0,133]）逐字陈述：元素加入/移除的次序被称为 last in, first out，并以首字母缩写 LIFO 指代。claim 的中文表述“后进先出（Last In, First Out，LIFO）”为该句的完整转译，无超出或偏离，故 supported。

supporting_quotes.exact: The order in which elements are added to or removed from a stack is described as last in, first out, referred to by the acronym LIFO.

observations.object: taking item off top; accessing deeper datum may require removing multiple other items first
observations.subject: stack

claims.rationale: 引文（区间 [0,198]）以实物堆叠为喻：从栈顶取项容易（easy to take an item off the top），访问更深数据可能需要先移除多个其他项。claim 各分句与该句一一对应，为忠实转译，故 supported。

supporting_quotes.exact: As with a stack of physical objects, this structure makes it easy to take an item off the top of the stack, but accessing a datum deeper in the stack may require removing multiple other items first.

observations.object: value of last element added (item at top of stack)
observations.subject: peek operation

claims.rationale: 引文（区间 [0,142]）明确：peek 可在不修改栈的情况下返回最后加入元素的值，即栈顶项。claim 的“不修改栈的情况下返回最后加入元素的值（栈顶项）”与引文完全一致，故 supported。

supporting_quotes.exact: Additionally, a peek operation can, without modifying the stack, return the value of the last element added (the item at the top of the stack).

observations.predicate: has one end (top) as only push/pop position
observations.subject: stack

claims.rationale: 引文（区间 [0,195]）说明：作为顺序集合，栈只有一端（栈顶）是 push 与 pop 唯一可发生的位置，另一端（栈底）固定。claim 的三要素——顺序集合、栈顶唯一操作位置、栈底固定——全部由引文支撑，故 supported。

supporting_quotes.exact: Considered a sequential collection, a stack has one end which is the only position at which the push and pop operations may occur, the top of the stack, and is fixed at the other end, the bottom.

observations.object: stack overflow when full and not enough space for another element; bounded capacity
observations.predicate: is in a state of / may be implemented to have
observations.subject: stack

claims.rationale: 引文（区间 [0,179]）指出：栈可实现为有界容量；当栈已满且没有足够空间接受另一元素时，处于 stack overflow 状态。claim 中“有界容量”“已满且无足够空间”“栈溢出状态”逐项对应引文，故 supported。

supporting_quotes.exact: A stack may be implemented to have a bounded capacity. If the stack is full and does not contain enough space to accept another element, the stack is in a state of stack overflow.

observations.object: array or linked list (special case of a list); interface not implementation; user only allowed to pop/push
observations.predicate: can be implemented via / identified by
observations.subject: stack

observations.object: a singly linked list with a pointer to the top element
observations.subject: stack

claims.rationale: 引文一（区间 [0,335]）支撑：栈可轻易用数组或链表实现，是 list 特例；标识栈的是接口而非实现，用户仅被允许 pop/push（有少量其他辅助操作）。引文二（区间 [0,100]）补充示例：可用指向栈顶元素的单链表实现。两条引文互为补充、无冲突，共同完整支撑 claim 的所有分句，故 supported。

supporting_quotes.exact: A stack can be easily implemented either through an array or a linked list, as it is merely a special case of a list. In either case, what identifies the data structure as a stack is not the implementation but the interface: the user is only allowed to pop or push items onto the array or linked list, with few other helper operations.
A stack may be implemented as, for example, a singly linked list with a pointer to the top element.

observations.predicate: adds element and increments top index after checking overflow
observations.subject: push operation

observations.predicate: decrements top index after checking underflow, returns previously top item
observations.subject: pop operation

claims.rationale: 引文一（区间 [0,93]）：push 在检查溢出后添加元素并递增 top 索引；引文二（区间 [0,124]）：pop 在检查下溢后递减 top 索引并返回此前位于栈顶的项。两条引文分别精确对应 claim 的 push/pop 两句，无冲突，故 supported。

supporting_quotes.exact: The push operation adds an element and increments the top index, after checking for overflow:
Similarly, pop decrements the top index after checking for underflow, and returns the item that was previously the top one:

observations.object: RPN calculators holding values; prefix/postfix/infix representation and conversion; compiler syntax parsing before low-level translation
observations.subject: stack

claims.rationale: 引文（区间 [0,312]）三句话分别支撑 claim 的“逆波兰计算器用栈保存值”“表达式可用前缀/后缀/中缀表示且可经栈转换”“编译器在翻译为低级代码前用栈解析语法”，每句均被对应覆盖，无超出，故 supported。

supporting_quotes.exact: Calculators that employ reverse Polish notation use a stack structure to hold values. Expressions can be represented in prefix, postfix or infix notations and conversion from one form to another may be accomplished using a stack. Many compilers use a stack to parse syntax before translation into low-level code.

observations.object: pushing last correct point onto stack, popping in case of incorrect path
observations.subject: backtracking

claims.rationale: 引文一（区间 [0,56]）声明栈的另一个重要应用是回溯；引文二（区间 [0,157]，其中 This 指代引文一的 backtracking）说明：把最后正确的点压入栈，路径错误时从栈中弹出（即回到该点）。两条引文互补覆盖 claim 全部内容，故 supported。

supporting_quotes.exact: Another important application of stacks is backtracking.
This can be achieved through the use of stacks, as a last correct point can be pushed onto the stack, and popped from the stack in case of an incorrect path.

observations.predicate: implemented directly in hardware / fixed-depth not directly accessible
observations.subject: stacks

claims.rationale: 引文（区间 [0,175]）指出：有相当数量小型微处理器直接在硬件中实现栈，部分微控制器有不可直接访问的定深（fixed-depth）栈。claim 的“不少小型微处理器直接硬件实现栈”与“一些微控制器有不可直接访问的定深栈”均被对应支撑，故 supported。

supporting_quotes.exact: There is also a number of small microprocessors that implement a stack directly in hardware, and some microcontrollers have a fixed-depth stack that is not directly accessible.
